    The crimes of Russell Brand - podcast
    In the decades he’s spent on screens, Russell Brand’s been a comedian, an actor, a presenter and a political anarchist. Now he has been convicted of rape and sexual assaults. Emine Sinmaz reports We’ve seen many iterations of Russell Brand. Camp Camden goth. Outrageous standup and TV host. Hollywood star. Political anarchist. Reborn Christian conspiracy theorist. Brand always wanted to be famous. And when he attained celebrity in the 2000s, he was seen as a breath of fresh air. Hyper-camp, hyper-sexual, hyper-articulate, he was considered edgy by TV and radio commissioners and funnier than anyone else by his fans. A Guardian columnist and the Sun’s shagger of the year, Brand was supposed to be ironic, a pop culture provocateur, journalist Sophie Heawood tells Nosheen Iqbal. But in the past decade, it’s become harder to remember why he was so celebrated. Continue reading...  ( 12 min )
